newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Siemens VT unit seeks profit turnaround.
newsitem.headline: Siemens VT unit seeks profit turnaround.

text.p: German industrial giant Siemens AG said on Tuesday said its locomotive unit, expecting a small loss in 1996/97, hoped a reorganisation would lead to profit of five percent return on sales by 2000.
Siemens transport technology (VT) chief Wolfram Martinsen said a plan to cut jobs in Germany this year could make a profit in 1997/98 possible.
VT, as part of its plan to raise profit, would also partner with competitors in projects overseas to break into new markets, especially in Asia, Martinsen said.

Job cuts in Germany would include a 30 percent reduction in the unit's headquarters staff, he said. At the same time, VT would add staff overseas, resulting in a net reduction of about 200 jobs and a worldwide head count of about 12,800.
The cost-cutting plan, the unit's second reorganisation within the last few years, would enable VT "to achieve positive results again," Martinsen said.
With General Motors Corp., Siemens would market diesel-electric locomotives. With ADtranz, it was cooperating on public transportation systems for Shanghai and Guangzhou areas in China.

Outside of Europe and North America, Siemens and France's GEC Alsthom would use market their high-speed rail technology together, he said. Siemens developed Germany's ICE trains, while GEC Alsthom produced France's TGV technology.
